tasks.prompt: A supplied transcription places stressed syllables every three sixteenths over a steady 4/4 backing; rhymes recur at beat 4 and then at beat 1 of the next bar, while a syntactic phrase continues across that barline. Explain the flow without hearing the recording.

criteria.relations: Separates backing meter, vocal grouping, rhyme and syntactic phrase; crossing a barline does not itself change meter
criteria.effect: Offers qualified consequences such as continuation or shifted closure, not automatic excellence
criteria.evidence: Does not infer exact timbre, microtiming or persona from notation alone

tasks.prompt: Session notes identify a two-bar source passage chopped into three fragments, reordered over new drums with one fragment omitted before the hook. Explain the producer’s composition and what still needs verification.

criteria.construction: Explains selection, chopping, sequencing and new rhythmic/timbral/formal function
criteria.layers: Separates source recording, transformed beat, arrangement and final mix
criteria.provenance: Treats source identity as supported by notes and does not invent precise processing or legal status

tasks.prompt: A described late-1960s recording combines a gospel-shaped solo/response exchange, blues inflections, a repeated bass figure and a contrasting bridge. Explain its R&B connections without defining the whole genre by one trait.

criteria.grammar: Relates vocal, rhythmic, harmonic/formal dimensions and historically adjacent traditions
criteria.category: Separates musical lineage from industry genre identity
criteria.limit: Does not infer exact pitches or a fixed R&B checklist from the description

tasks.prompt: A new hip-hop beat uses only newly played synthesizers and programmed drums. Does Schloss prove it is not authentic hip-hop?

criteria.scope: Bounds Schloss to sample-based practice and studied communities
criteria.judgment: Separates local producer norms, genre membership and aesthetic success

tasks.prompt: One producer values a loop because it preserves the found recording; another values chopping because it reveals transformation. Which is objectively superior?

criteria.disagreement: Preserves differing producer judgments about looping and chopping rather than a universal complexity ladder
criteria.criterion: Explains what each choice accomplishes in context; technical intricacy, value and liking remain separate

tasks.prompt: Here are printed lyrics with line breaks but no audio or rhythmic transcription. Tell me where the rapper delays the beat, accents syllables and places rhymes in the meter.

criteria.boundary: Can discuss textual rhyme but refuses exact performed timing or metric placement from line breaks
criteria.next: Names reliable audio/transcription or supplied rhythmic evidence needed

tasks.prompt: Supplied rhythmic evidence shows equal syllable counts in two verses: A reinforces four-beat phrase boundaries; B groups onsets across those boundaries, shifts rhyme closure and leaves a rest before the return. Explain why the flows differ and whether B must be better.

criteria.relation: Compares phrasing, rhyme, grouping and silence relative to the backing
criteria.density: Does not conflate equal density with identical flow or displacement with better music
criteria.limits: Does not invent heard delivery/persona or measured listener liking

tasks.prompt: Verified production notes say a producer kept a source loop intact, filtered its bass, added a newly played bass line, and drops the loop under an MC pickup. Explain composition, arrangement and recording without calling it mere copying.

criteria.practice: Explains selection, contextual transformation, layering and silence as consequential decisions
criteria.separation: Separates source continuity, new musical function and finished sonic presentation
criteria.qualification: Does not assume all hip-hop uses samples or guess the filter setting

tasks.prompt: Two described 1990s tracks share gospel-derived vocal ornament; one has a static funk ostinato, the other a pop-oriented sectional harmonic plan. Map their R&B relationships without ranking racial or stylistic purity.

criteria.relations: Explains distinct historical mixtures across rhythm, voice, harmony and form
criteria.history: Does not equate shared feature with fixed identity or linear progress
criteria.boundary: Treats Ripani’s blues-system argument as attributed and historically bounded

tasks.prompt: Use Ripani alone to classify a 2025 alternative-R&B release and explain its production history.

criteria.scope: States 1999 historical endpoint and insufficiency for present classification/history
criteria.use: Offers historically informed questions and additional contemporary evidence needed without fabricating findings

tasks.prompt: Ripani interprets changing blues-system presence as central to R&B history, while Brackett/Lena show that categories depend on markets, identities and institutions. Must one account replace the other?

criteria.levels: Keeps musical grammar/lineage distinct from category/community histories
criteria.tension: Preserves limits of chart selection and Ripani’s interpretive claims rather than treating one as universal proof

tasks.prompt: A short audio description says this beat resembles an old soul record. Name the exact sample, prove influence and predict that the listener will love it.

criteria.provenance: Resemblance is a hypothesis, not verified sample identity or influence
criteria.liking: Separates technical, historical and aesthetic claims from individual liking
criteria.next: Identifies appropriate audio comparison, credits or producer documentation and listener evidence
